_notes.voiceId: Resolved from voiceName via GET /v1/voices on first use and cached here, so every later run is one fewer request and is pinned to the voice that was actually used.
_notes.languageCode: The corpus is English, so every request says so. Without it a multilingual model infers the language from the text, and a short entry gives it almost nothing to go on. Sent only for models that accept it.
_notes.outputFormat: ElevenLabs bills characters, not bytes -- output format does not change the price. So this generates at the highest the plan allows and scripts/package-audio.sh transcodes down if the download is too large. Generating small to save money would save nothing and make a later quality bump a second purchase.
_notes.dictionaryId: An ElevenLabs pronunciation dictionary to apply. The generator resolves its latest version at the start of every run and uses that for the whole run -- the lexicon is edited in ../wow-voiceover and this project always wants its newest version. Each take records the version it was made with, so drift stays knowable per line. Setting dictionaryVersionId here would act as a pin and skip the per-run resolution. Phoneme rules are honoured by eleven_v3 and eleven_flash_v2 only, which is one more reason this project is on v3.
_notes.creditRate: Credits per character. ElevenLabs bills round(characters x rate) and the rate belongs to the plan, not the request. Measured at 0.607 over the first 44 generated lines on this account with eleven_v3 -- an earlier 0.55 taken from the sibling project understated the bill by 10%. Only a fallback: once the manifest holds generated lines the estimate is measured from those instead, and the character-cost response header is always authoritative.
_notes.stability: v3 exposes this as Creative (0.0) / Natural (0.5) / Robust (1.0). Natural, because Creative hallucinates across an unattended run of 1353 clips and Robust gives up the expressiveness v3 was chosen for.
